_howTo: Radio talks with Walla Walla, typed out on the slip. Each lesson has two: "start" comes on as the lesson opens, and "check" is a short quiz once the lesson's check is done. Each talk has turns; in each turn Walla Walla says "them" and the player picks one of up to three "replies" (none means a plain "Roger. Over."). A reply can have a "back" line, and "right": true marks the right answer to a question (it is never scored). Every reply leads on to the next turn.

turns.them: Harrow, Walla Walla. Harvest is near, and cut wheat can’t sit wet, so this week’s question is a practical one: how much warning can you get of rain? Often a day, if you look up high.

replies.back: Sometimes more. The ice clouds out in front tell you what’s coming long before it gets here.

turns.them: The high floor, all ice, the grey sheets that come down after it, and a ring around the sun. Questions at the end.
Harrow, Walla Walla. Questions. There’s a ring round the sun. Hold your hand out at arm’s length: about how far is it from the sun to the ring?

replies.back: Twenty-two degrees, a spread hand at arm’s length. Every halo, every time.
Much bigger than that. Twenty-two degrees is a whole spread hand at arm’s length.
That’s the beauty of it: it never does. The crystals bend the light by the same 22 degrees every time.

turns.them: A warm front is on its way. In what order do its clouds arrive?

replies.say: High clouds first, then middle, then low.
replies.back: Top down, like a lid closing. Each step means the front is that much closer.
Backwards. The warm air slides up over the cold along a long, gentle slope, so the highest clouds arrive first, far out ahead.
Then nobody would get any warning. High first, then middle, then low.

turns.them: The sun is a dim disc, as if behind frosted glass, and shadows have gone. Which cloud?

replies.back: Right. Rain in a few hours, likely.
Cirrostratus leaves the sun sharp, with shadows and maybe a halo. Frosted glass is altostratus.
Nimbostratus hides the sun entirely. A dim disc is altostratus.

turns.them: Now you can give a farmer a timetable instead of a shrug. Next lesson, thunderstorms.
